name: Org Strategy Governance Models
description: Governance structures recommended for single-org and multi-org Salesforce deployments in pharma/life sciences. Covers CoE, review boards, tiered administration, and chargeback models.
source: Org Strategy And Design — Salesforce Life Sciences

governance_stack.description: Layered governance model. All layers are needed for single-org with multiple LOBs. Multi-org requires per-org instances of layers 2-4 plus a global CoE.

layers.name: Global Center of Excellence (CoE)
responsibilities: Manage business architecture and common standards across all orgs
Design and maintain a Reference Architecture defining when additional orgs are justified
Coordinate and create awareness of the entire Salesforce community in the company
Organize workshops with enterprise data architects to prevent data duplication across orgs
Serve as the governance committee in single-org environments

layers.name: Per-Org Governance Committee
responsibilities: Manage product direction and set priorities within the org
Define specific roles and responsibilities within the org
Create and maintain a RACI matrix for all types of changes
Balance competing LOB demands for shared resources

layers.name: Architectural Review Board
responsibilities: Actively design, review, and approve all technical changes
Review all configuration changes, data model changes, and custom code
Enforce naming standards and separation of concerns
Ensure technical architect reviews all aspects of the org

tiers.name: LOB Business SME
tiers.description: Delegated admin privileges for operational tasks
tiers.note: Business SMEs work directly in production for non-technical changes

tiers.name: Single Service Desk
tiers.description: Centralized entry point across all orgs
capabilities: Triage and route all Salesforce support requests
tiers.note: One service desk for all orgs ensures consistent SLA

tiers.name: Per-Org Support Team
tiers.description: Dedicated troubleshooting and escalation per org

tiers.name: Platform Engineering / Architects
tiers.description: Deep technical expertise for cross-cutting concerns

chargeback_model.description: Funding model for multi-LOB Salesforce deployments.
chargeback_model.principle: Charge back support costs to business units by establishing a license tax.
guidelines: Larger LOBs may fund and support their own org
Smaller LOBs pool resources around the centralized CoE
Each LOB funds their own development resources proportional to usage
Shared infrastructure costs (integration platform, data warehouse) are centrally funded

profile_first_principle.description: The single most important org strategy recommendation: always evaluate whether splitting profiles resolves the issue before splitting orgs.
profile_first_principle.rationale: Profiles provide LOB-level autonomy within a shared org at a fraction of the cost and complexity of org splitting. Profile splitting preserves: shared data model, shared integrations, shared reporting, shared governance — while giving each LOB its own: page layouts, field-level security, record type access, app visibility, and tab access.
when_profile_split_is_insufficient: Hard platform limits are exceeded (custom objects, permission sets, Apex code size)
Data residency laws require physical data isolation
Regulatory requirements prevent any data sharing between BUs
Maintenance window conflicts cannot be resolved by profile-based deployment
